conf.description: apache-httpd access dataset, json format (mod_log_config JSON LogFormat template). Mechanism is elastic-ingest-pipeline (a custom logs-apache.access@custom pipeline), not the stock apache integration grok, so this format is parsed here in Cribl: JSON-extract _raw, rename the ASF example template's keys to ECS, and apply the field-table transforms. Field names follow the map's illustrative LogFormat JSON template ({"@timestamp":...,"client_ip":"%a",...}); an operator's actual key names are LogFormat-defined and may differ.

conf.comment: apache-httpd / access / json: mod_log_config JSON LogFormat line. Parsed here (not deferred) because the map's mechanism for this format is elastic-ingest-pipeline (a custom Elastic pipeline replacing the stock apache-integration grok), so there is no stock grok to fight. Keys below match the map's illustrative template: @timestamp, client_ip, user, method, path, query, protocol, status, resp_bytes, bytes_in, bytes_out, duration_us, vhost, port, referer, user_agent, xff.

functions.description: document parsing rationale and assumed key names
decode the mod_log_config JSON line into fields
batch-rename every status: mapped field to its ECS target (@timestamp already matches its ECS name and needs no rename)

apply field-table transforms: strip leading ? from url.query, strip HTTP/ prefix from http.version, convert %D microseconds to event.duration nanoseconds, derive event.outcome from the status code, tag event.dataset, and copy the @timestamp value into a plain-named temp field (Cribl's field-name validator rejects '@' in a dedicated field-name parameter, so auto_timestamp cannot read '@timestamp' directly)
parse the ISO-8601 timestamp into Cribl's internal event time; the original @timestamp field is left untouched for Elastic
drop the temp field used only to work around the @timestamp field-name limitation
